title: GIDA IS A MIXED PUBLIC-PRIVATE COMPANY: ISN'T THAT STRANGE? WHY SUCH A "HYBRID" REALITY?
answer: It is not strange even if quite unusual on the Italian scene. In any case, it is a positive and virtuous aspect of the company, which deals with both civil and industrial drains making all those who produce them, citizens and companies, co-responsible. Today, we talk more and more often about public-private synergies, we can say that GIDA has been ahead of its time. The mixed solution emerged naturally, so to speak, when the Merli Law (1976) imposed a path to make wastewater purification mandatory: the Municipality of Prato (as majority shareholder) and the Unione Industriale Pratese were in fact the subjects called into question and the only ones who had and could activate the necessary resources. In 2004 Consiag was added to them, so today the shareholding structure is composed as follows: Municipality of Prato (46.92%); Unione Industriale Pratese (45.08%); Consiag (8%). In the "About Us" section of our website you will find out more about the company's history, mission and governance.
